title: The Overlap Gap Property: Separating Quantum and Quantum-Inspired Approximate Optimization Algorithms
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the Mean-Field Approximate Optimization Algorithm (MF-AOA), a quantum-inspired classical algorithm of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), is unable to give arbitrary near optimal solution for problems exhibiting the Overlap Gap Property (OGP). We show this by relating the MF-AOA to finite-memory Approximate Message Passing (AMP) algorithms, which are known to be limited in performance by the OGP. Thus, our paper argues that problems exhibiting the OGP are one such instance where the QAOA can outperform the MF-AOA and AMP algorithms in general. We supplement this by numerically simulating the performance of the QAOA on instances of Max-$4$-XORSAT that exhibit the OGP and find that the QAOA is able to surpass the barrier, while our finite-size scaling analysis favors a super-polynomial over a polynomial depth dependence. In addition, we observe a non-differentiable point in the performance of the QAOA near by the OGP barrier, where the optimal QAOA parameters change from an adiabatic to a non-adiabatic schedule.
summary: This paper proves that the classical mean-field approximation of QAOA (MF-AOA) fails for problems exhibiting the Overlap Gap Property (OGP). By simulating QAOA on such instances, the authors argue that QAOA can potentially surpass this algorithmic barrier, suggesting a super-polynomial advantage over classical methods, while also identifying a critical transition point in the optimal parameter schedule.
main_problem: To prove that the Mean-Field Approximate Optimization Algorithm (MF-AOA), a quantum-inspired classical algorithm derived from QAOA, cannot find near-optimal solutions for problems exhibiting the Overlap Gap Property (OGP).
main_result: The paper shows that while QAOA might surpass the OGP barrier, MF-AOA is fundamentally limited by it, and the advantage of QAOA over classical/mean-field approaches is suggested to be super-polynomial in depth.
method: The authors relate MF-AOA to finite-memory Approximate Message Passing (AMP) algorithms and use numerical simulations and finite-size scaling analysis on Max-4-XORSAT instances.
model_or_system: The study focuses on combinatorial optimization problems, specifically Max-q-XORSAT, analyzed through the lens of QAOA and its classical mean-field approximation (MF-AOA). The OGP is a topological property characterizing the difficulty of finding near-optimal solutions.
key_observables: Approximation ratio ($F_p$), overlap distribution $P(q)$, and the required circuit depth ($p$) to overcome the OGP barrier.
important_parameters: The Overlap Gap Property (OGP) itself, the depth $p$, and the comparison between adiabatic and non-adiabatic parameter schedules.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on relating MF-AOA to AMP algorithms and assumes the existence of the OGP for certain problem classes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometric manifestation of OGP (disconnected solution space) and show the performance separation between QAOA on OGP vs. non-OGP instances, along with the identification of a non-differentiable point in QAOA performance.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical limitation of MF-AOA due to OGP by linking it to AMP algorithms. It then uses numerical simulations on Max-4-XORSAT to demonstrate QAOA's potential advantage, including analyzing the transition between adiabatic and non-adiabatic parameter regimes near the OGP barrier.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding when quantum algorithms might offer a genuine advantage over their classical, mean-field approximations, particularly in the presence of structural barriers like the OGP.
